Find the area $A$ bounded by the polar curve $r=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\theta )$ for $-\frac{\pi }{6}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{6},$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $r(\theta )=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\theta )$, ${\theta }_{1}=-\frac{\pi }{6}$ and ${\theta }_{2}=\frac{\pi }{6}.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\theta ))}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2{\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}{cos}^{2}⁡(3\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =(\theta +\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡(6\theta )){|}_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6} \\  & =(\frac{\pi }{6}-(-\frac{\pi }{6}))+\frac{1}{6}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi -\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\pi )) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}+0 \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
